reviews.text: My now wife and I watched the entirety of BSG in our early dating life together. I have all the minisodes and series ripped to my media drives and often rewatch it while grinding MMOs. I love BSG:Deadlock on steam, but it takes a lot more focus and time than a burnt out dad often has to throw at a game; one battle in that game can take 40+min, where here i beat several battles and did the inbetween upgrading and promotions in the same time. (completed the tutorial) As such, i was BEYOND stoked when i saw a *roguelike* rts Battlestar game coming... doubled down on that excitement when I saw it was the devs behind Crying Suns.! Needless to say, i had this game bought and installed about 3minutes after 9am MST, when it dropped. I've only beat the tutorial, but she's a frakking beauty so far; The pixel graphic detailing on the 3D modeled ships and ship consoles is a really cool artstyle decision,.. gives it a retro vibe while remaining fresh AND all in that delicious BSG flavor. So far very impressed.. the opening cutscene sampling the show's choir opening perfectly set the stage for something i'm sure will eat many hours of my life. It's also something that *demands* less from me at a time and is easier to step away and come back to, than other BSG titles. Might be my new fav BSG game.. SO SAY WE ALL

It's something else with a BSG title, it should have been called: B*llsh*t Galactica: Scattered Fanfics/Fanfic Hopes. The nonsense aside - in the game, this game still has potential, though I've barely scratched the surface. IDK why they went for a BSG skin though when they could have made something else standalone if they aren't going to stay even relatively(?) true to BSG. It's like the writer/publisher found a singular or several dozen obscure fanfics and just smoked a line of crack with the IP holder and somehow got permission to slap them all together without regard. What's that? The raptor is a slow, robust support shuttle? It had a variant with missile pods? NAH! FKN SLAP A RAIL GUN ON IT AND MAKE IT A SNIPER! Bar whoever smoked the crack and came up with these ridiculous ideas, the art and dev team went to town and made something interesting with depth. Good on em. Runs smooth, though I wish I had the choice for anti-aliasing. It's so bad at 1080p.

Every time I hear the Dradis contact sound I immediately hear Mr. Gaeta's voice in my head alerting me to the cylons. A very fun game that takes aspects of FTL, and applies them to the BSG (remake) universe, while also addinging a tactical part to the battle at the end of each sector before you jump. Can feel quite challenging at times to protect the fleet during those fights, but that is just part of the overwhelming threat that is the Cylons. It is truly a fight to survive and they capture that very well in this game. Definitely recommend this game to fans of the BSG remake.

I think I’ll give this game a thumbs up simply because it wasn’t awful, doesn’t feel like a rippoff, isn’t overprice and isn’t broken or unplayable. But it’s not anything super extraordinary or amazing. If you passed on it you wouldn’t miss much. It doesn’t add anything to the Battlestar Lore, it doesn’t offer groundbreaking gameplay, it doesn’t offer groundbreaking sound design or graphical design or anything really. The overall quality I could call it is average. It’s a very average game. It may be the MOST average of all average games because of how average it is. It’s not a rip off though. It’s not horrible or anything. I guess if you’re a fan of the IP and roguelikes you’ll probably get a kick out of it for a while. Just don’t come into this expecting some intense in-depth gameplay with story and choices or strategy or anything. Cuz it’s not that. It’s not bad (which is why I give it a thumbs up) but it’s not phenomenal either. I mean its graphics are okay but probably a good choice for what kind of game it is. The gameplay is okay, it’s fun enough I suppose. The sound design is okay, no voice acting, decent sound effects but great music. The stability was pretty good though other than a few framerate drops. Its UI, tutorial and price are appropriate. Its writing could use some work though. Regardless, it’s a perfectly average game. If that’s enough for you then I hope you enjoy it. However if you’d like more information then I encourage you to check out my review on YouTube (link below). https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zcclMWuK9F0 Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I was able to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

I want to start off by saying I am an uber BSG fan. I have an arm and back full of BSG tats, a couple of shelving units of ships and props, etc. I have a "FRAK" vanity plate on my car. I've played every BSG video and board game out there. I played through the demo at least 6-10 times. It was tough in spots but not too rough. I put 6 hours into the game today/tonight. I am at Level 5+ bonuses. Even then, the difficulty level of the game is impossible. I am nowhere close to making it through with the 1st fleet and unlocking another option, let alone seeing how the game can be beat. (EDIT: I didn't get my 1st "win" until Level 6, and Level 7-8 was eventually where I could comfortably beat runs. This takes double-digit hours.) First, the game is very, very loosely related to the series. You start off with a Viper Mk 2 and Raptor, but the Raptor doesn't in any way resemble even the combat Raptors from the series. The Mk 7 and Blackbird eventually pop up. However, everything else is made up or "noncanon" (i.e., no Mk3 from Blood and Chrome, etc.). There is a loose mention of Adama and BSG being at the "end of the run", but that's it. None of the "made up" ships that appear in the game appear to be in any way spin-offs or related to ships that appear in the series. The devs could've call the game anything without paying for the BSG license and it wouldn't have changed. (EDIT: I eventually acquired a ship called the Cobra. The Cobra is identical to the Combat Raptors from the series. However, despite being able to call one ship a Raptor, they can't call this one the proper name of the Combat Raptor? Did the devs and testers even watch the entire series?) The characters for each playthrough appear to be randomly generated. I swear on one playthrough the XO and CAG were the same dang face/facial hair/person, so there's that too. (EDIT: It doesn't get any better. There was one playthrough where an A.A. male and a white female looked identical except their skin color and hair.) Nevertheless, I still wanted to like the game and the experience. After a short time, the constant pop-ups from challenges and other opportunities gets to the point where I wanted to slam my head in a car door. There is no way to keep up with getting resources and the challenges. Assign a crew member to get tylium? Here's another pop up event. Then, assign a crew member to gather scrap? Here's another pop up event. You can't do anything for more than a turn or two without another pop up out of nowhere. (EDIT: To make it worse, these events have no variety. The same events occur under the same circumstances every playthrough. E.g., does your Underworld rating drop to tense? The inflation event pops up almost immediately.) The difficulty level reminds me of a "free to play" but "pay to keep up/win" mobile game where even optimal play won't allow you to keep up with how bad you are getting whacked, except this game does not have those mobile "pay to get more resources or turns" options. There was a BSG mobile game like this. Thus far, I cannot find any redeeming qualities unless you want to flush $20 down the toilet for something with the BSG name on it. The game is very loosely related to BSG, the graphics aren't great, there is little variety, the difficulty level is impossible, etc.; most importantly, I had 0 fun playing it and found 0 redeeming qualities. I wasted an evening and $20. Don't repeat my mistake EDIT: I wanted to give this a chance b/c I love BSG so much, but my initial review still holds and more. Now, I find out that 1 of the 4 fleets, the 2nd one, won't unlock, and the devs didn't address it in the initial patch. Some people in the discussions think it has to do w/ the save file coming over from the demo.

I'm still on the fence about this game, but as of release I can't recommend it due to bugs and jank. I think there is the concept of a good game here, but it's not here yet. The tutorial was extremely slow and boring, but I was having more fun after I got into a tough battle and barely survived. I like pixel art, and low-poly art, but there's such a weird mash-up of pixel art, low poly models, and detailed hand-painted art that it doesn't look cohesive. The way the ships are animated also looks jank. Ships slide around with zero weight or consideration for physics. Not just in battle, but in the scenes that play out behind your menu. One of the coolest things about the show was how ships moved and they did not capture that at all. Even for a game it looks bad. I ran into bugs where the character portraits were missing, replaced with a white image. Speaking of menus, they are all so slow. Switching to the hanger, bar, or R&D need a loading screen. Dialogue scenes are inconsistent. You click to advance the text, but sometimes a button will popup in the middle of the screen right under my mouse and I will click it without reading it. Most of the buttons pop up on the right side of the screen. Sound design seems almost completely absent. The game opens to the absolute banger of the BSG theme song, which does a great job of setting hyping me up, but that after, there's barely any sound in the game at all.

It's not that great. No new mechanics. Nothing new brought to the genre. It feels like the Battlestar name was just used as a hook to suck fans of the IP into buying. Almost any SciFi IP can be thrown onto this game with a bit of a facelift (changing the design of the ships & sound effects) and it wouldn't change anything. It also has a very mobile game feel to it. I had high hopes for this game, as Battlestar Galactica is one of my favorite IPs of all time. What a let down.

It's more like an FTL but you play as a small fleet. You have survival elements and combat elements. The survival elements mean managing resources, morale and weapons. The combat is defending the ships with an active pause. I played 1 hour here but the next episode i restarted on the Veteran difficulty, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XCoPPb92LLo The game has permanent upgrades that make runs easier and unlocks for new stuff and new starting fleets(there are 4 in total). The game has massive potential, the only thing that slows it down is the janky dialogue and events that slow down the gameplay to a crawl. The balance is pretty good but sometimes a run is made or broken by the RNG of the first upgrades so it feels like you should restart until later when we unlock more things.

If you like getting kicked in the ♥♥♥♥, buy this game otherwise youre wasting your time, it is literally designed to waste your time. I will finish this out of spite, but ill hate every second.

Devs did good job at trying to simulate the BSG gamedesign, but everything else feels just bad. Cons: 1) I have beaten the game on highest difficulty, but when farming achievements I changed to easiest one, and the difficulty difference was marginal. The game will be very hard for casual players. 2) For readability reasons, game uses individual units representing squadrons, instead of actual squadrons. This however takes away from the BSG feeling of fighters engaging in combat. 3) Game makes heavy use of extended lore ships, which will not spark nostalgy, unless you are familiar with it. 4) Balance is very much off. Your fighters will have 100+ dps, while your battleship will have weapons with 10-20 dps. Even a nuke has a dps of 30 (yeah it's big AOE, but that's it) A lot of perks of higher tiers are weak, while some common perks are S-tier 5) Combat does not have much of depth to it. Destroying enemy capships gives you a tiny resource bonus, but there is no gameplay change (e.g. I would expect the level to autowin, if I kill a capital ship. Instead game goes on, like nothing happened) 6) Low replayability due to everything feeling same. Total number of fighters is limited, but even those do not feel different. A far greater difference commes from perks you roll, but otherwise you pretty much have only 2 ships (fighters & support) SPOILER 7) If you kill final boss, literally nothing happens. You kill the basestar, but do not get even a dialogue option. No, you still get the same cinematic, as you ram that very basestar, you have just killed with conventional weapons. You do get an achievement, but the fact that game straight out ignores your actions in such a pivotal moment, made me close the game and stop playing. SPOILER Pros: 1) Gamedesign of what happens between fights. There are plenty of quests which make it feel like actual BSG thing. Albeit it does become tedious very fast. 2) If you plan on doing 2-3 runs, the game will likely be fun to you. A single run lasts 2-4 hours, so you are getting about 5-12 hours of fun content in BSG theme. 3) Game appears to be stable. 4) Game has achievements.

This game bills itself as a rogue-like space game, in the rough template of FTL, and obviously, Crying Suns (from the same developer.) It is that, in that you jump from system to system, with a tactical battle in between, and you carefully manage resources and enhance your combat craft to try to reach the Galactica's fleet to succeed your run. The actual managing of resources and play is engaging, and the Battlestar Galactica is a pull for people who remember and love that franchise. The game falls over for being unduly punishing, though. And to that end, I'm not talking about the difficulty; that can be tailored with some accuracy. It is more that the UI is hostile in a way that simply isn't acceptable for a supposedly strategy-based roguelike. The slick graphics and the repeated crises (drawing from a pool of only a few dozen, you'll see all of them within a few hours of play) invites the player to click through, but it is far too easy to click on an interface element that hasn't appeared yet, making the decision for you more or less at random. As many other reviews have mentioned, there's usually a clear "best" option, and because of the snowball nature of these games, those mis-clicks are not confirmed, and not reversible. It is *very* easy to turn a perfectly viable run into a failure that will take two hours to play out with a poor menu selection. Likewise, the combat suffers from similar issues. Although the screen is pausible, it is not zoomable, and in the graphics-intense, densely piled groups of fighters that the game throws at you, it can be difficult, even in freeze-frame, to see what's happening. It can also be outright impossible to target the unit you need to target if other units, hostile or friendly, are atop it. Nominally this wouldn't be a tremendous issue, but the game routinely throws support units that give enemies 40% damage reduction, or 90% evasion at you, requiring a specific order to tactics that sometimes simply can't be employed due to the interface. Finally, the game also does not allow undo doing pause for some mis-clicks. Like many RTS games, left-click is select, right-click is command. However, right-click also un-deploys weapons and fighters. Many weapons, such as the flak barrage from the player's ship take thirty seconds to redeploy once undeployed. The practical upshot is that a simple mis-click of weapon systems can scrub a run entirely and irrevocably, which is simply not acceptable for a game where a run can take from 60 to 150 minutes. All told, this game seems like it has a solid core, utterly undone by an unforgiving interface and obnoxious controls. I'm certain that once this game was played for dozens of hours, these issues would become learned out of the player, but I beg of you not to commit that much time to this game. We need to expect better of developers, and to be more respectful of players and their time in games that supposedly don't orient themselves around dexterity as a skill. I have no problem with control mastery games, and I enjoy them myself, but this is not one of those games, and the choice to frustrate and undermine the player the way the UX team has chosen to in this game is bewildering, and ultimately destroys the experience.

I'll say no, for now. TL;DR: it feels like the game is purposely designed to break immersion and make you question the game's design choices. There are complaints that the game is woke, with most officers being dark skin, and far more females than males in most runs. These complaints are true, but I focus on the character designs themselves regardless of skin color. Many of the character portraits have mottled skin, unnatural lines going down their face, and strange colorations like everybody is severely ill. The character generator seems to have 2 parts to the selection: face and arms as one part, and central body as another part. This means character torsos are very androgynous; women with thin arms have the chests of male body builders. This causes their bodies to have unnatural proportions, and they start to look grotesque after playing for a while. Most of the character portraits feel like they belong in a horror game, not a space survival roguelite. There are a lot of lore departures that have caused a lot of argument in the discussions. Most colonial fighters are new to this game, pulled from nowhere. The Raptor has a giant cannon attached, something never shown in the show, and could have been remedied by arming it with a type of missile instead. The Cylon ships are no better. Many fighters, like the dodger and hacker, are completely new to this game. The hacker ships fire EMP missiles which can temporarily stun your ships, including the Viper Mk II, which I believe is canonically immune. The gunstars are very contentious because they only existed in fan fiction until now, and their role in this game could have been taken up by smaller battlestars that already exist in the universe. Cylons have frigates, completely new, and searching online for their ship types brought up Star Trek results instead. Ultimately, the ships presented in-game spend more time violating the lore than catering to it, or trying to build upon it. Battles are arcadey, and many people complain that it feels like a mobile game. On top of that, the underlying CPU process is single-thread, so you'll have stuttering, a maxed-out single core, and all other cores untouched. The recommended CPU for the game is AMD's 9800X3D. The minimum is a 5800X. There's no optimization whatsoever, and I've seen no explanation why that is. Ship models are painfully barebones and blocky, but that's probably why the game can be played on a GTX1060 6GB, a GPU that's cheaper than the CPU. How? Why? Reasons. The crisis system, where random events happen in the days between major battles, is repetitive and frustrating. In the roughly 110 days it takes your fleet to get to the Galactica, you have to contend with criminals planting bombs on their own ship, workers striking, an STD outbreak, potentially multiple homicide cases, unstable nukes, a poorly-maintained jump drive, comms going down, an asteroid hit. There's a ship that leaks fuel because they were using the fuel tanks to smuggle weapons, and the captain left the weapons in the tanks for up to 90 days for reasons. There's a cylon spy, but the spy is random and their model usually won't resemble any of the humanoid cylons from the show. Each of these crises has consequences, like losing fuel every few days, or your ships take a lot more damage until the crisis is resolved. These crises can take days of focused effort to resolve in-game. I found myself frustrated at these crises, fantasizing about having options to abandon civilian ships or airlock responsible crew, and questioning why the ship captains can't resolve the issues themselves. It really felt like the only ones actually trying to reach the Galactica were my officers, the fighter pilots, and me. There's a level-up system for ships and officers! It's gamey, frustrating, and takes a giant dump on the lore. The creators of the 2004 BSG series explicitly aimed for realism. The developers of this game added death lasers. Most officer upgrades are useless; not in the way that some skills have a benefit but don't fit your intended character build, like other roguelites have done. They're useless in that their so niche they'll never get used (increase damage resistance each time this squad is wrecked), or their benefit is completely meaningless (increase officer max health by +1 and fully heal them). The squad upgrade system could be done away with entirely in favor of a flat +health/damage/speed/evasion or +damage/range/ability cooldown per level-up. Maybe keep in the auto-repair upgrades. The officer level-up system could also be scrapped entirely, and just increase base officer health from 3 to 4. There are some OP officer/squad upgrade combos that exist, but you're very unlikely to actually get them. Ultimately, the only thing the game has going for it is the name. If you strip out all the Battlestar Galactica content and replace it with new designs, this is a generic game cobbled together from parts randomly thrown together. It uses controversy and licenses a famous series to hide the fact that it's bland and forgettable.

I really, really want to like this game. But the amount of "Crises" you have to deal with, no thanks. After trying three runs, I'm done trying to save these people who want to kill themselves so badly.

I want to give this a positive review as the game loop is fun but so much time is wasted with forced click through dialogs even on fast mode. Each event is 5-8 screens of oneliners that I have to get through to make a decision. The thing is most of the time, possibly even all the time, the decision you make is not based on dialog but on which faction you offend or what outcome is better. After the 10th playthrough, you get a special crisis that gives you a special room: sure i'll click another 10 times just to be allowed to use the mechanic. This game needs a real fast mode that bypasses all the flavour text and lets me get on with the game. I stopped playing because the game got in the way of my playing it.
As a confirmed non-cylon, I can officially recommend this game to the humans of this world.

Kept trying, even on easiest - but this is ultimately the game; Ooo, this looks-CAPTAIN, THERE'S A CRISIS Maybe I'll try-CAPTAIN, THERE'S A CRISIS Right, well at least I can-CAPTAIN, THERE'S A CRISIS Ah, at least it says this sector is saf-CAPTAIN, THERE'S A CRISIS. FFS, now I've run out of-CAPTAIN, THERE'S A CRISIS You get given half a dozen 'crisis' before you even start the game, making the resources you start with pointless too. Fun for half an hour (so that reviewers will like it), but quickly because a pointless game of crisis-after-crisis with actual fights given as a reward once in a while...and even then, your fighters' AI is idiotic and will ignore major missiles sailing past them because they're attack a ship, even when your other fighters are attack the same ship. Find yourself a fun game, this ain't it. Oh and they just released the smallest patch I've ever seen, which makes the game even yet still more harder/ pointless to play.

This game is good and is pretty accurate to the show. People complaining about crises are just not very good at games I think. If you watch the show you understand that it is part of it. I will say it takes many runs to get to a point where you succeed fully. It is not an easy game but it is fun once you know what is going on. Makes me want to declare martial law within the fleet and - what's that buzzing noise?

我很喜欢太空堡垒卡拉狄加这个ip，不过感觉目前这几个游戏，之前的Deadlock和这个Scattered Hopes感觉都做得一般。 再说说这个游戏本身，我很喜欢这个工作室的美术风格，但是在游戏性方面实在是做得有些不得劲。这个工作室的上一作Crying Suns也类似这样，叙事和美术都很不错，但是实际玩起来很糟心。Scattered Hopes采用了和Crying Suns几乎相同的战斗系统，同样玩起来很膈应。 我不知道是不是还是按照那个思路，想模仿FTL，所以继续采用的这种即时战略+暂停的模式，不过也许是想做出太空堡垒卡拉狄加那种争分夺秒的感觉，但实际上这样的模式加上这个设定玩起来很折磨。我理想中的太空堡垒卡拉狄加的游戏应该是类似Into the Breach那种回合制战斗。 所以还是点个踩吧，目前内容也不多，玩了两局感觉玩不下去了。
It's a fun rougelike game, it has some ui problems and is a bit glitchy on my computer but overall its a really fun game. It captures the vibe from battlestar galactica and does a great job.

There is a good game in here. However, the crises are endless and not very well balanced. You spend every single turn dealing with the last crisis, only to have a "free" turn come up with an additional surprise crisis. On top of that, the faction "management" is, well, nearly unmanageable, as every choice either raises the influence of one faction, at the expense of decreasing the relationship of the opposing one. That leads to a "tense" relationship, wherein that particular faction(s) will sabotage the fleet, creating more crises. Thing is though, the only way to improve relationships, is to get a random encounter in the bar, which only happens once per cycle. That means if the RNG gods aren't on your side, well, sucks to be you. Giving resources or favor to one faction only increases their influence, and thus potential rewards, and punishments for pissing them off. By the end of it all, I'm just to the point where I don't care if any of these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ survives or not, which how much they're trying to kill themselves by sabotaging the fleet. There IS a good game in here, but the balancing is atrocious, the management, is non existent. I get it's supposed to create a sense of "the Cyclons are hot on our heels, we have no time to catch our breath", but when your own people are also actively trying to kill you, yea, it gets less fun to want to save them, or try again.

The gameplay is great, with some nice improvements from Crying Suns. And while the crises system could be interesting, I get a feeling of dread (and boredom) everytime yet another crises appear. The relentless wave of crises turn what could have been an interesting sub-system into a slog. I really want to like this game, the fights are much more interesting and dynamic than Crying Suns, which is why I keep reopening it. But then I get faced with too many crises. The vast majority of them are interesting, and the mechanics to deal with them is also fine. It's really the onslaught of messages and "dialogues" for each new crisis that turn the whole thing into a negative. Let me play the game, sheesh
The crisis system feels just tedious - not really adding to the gameplay at all. Always getting interrupted by yet another crisis does not feel fun at all.

This game does not respect your time in the slightest. Be prepared for worse RNG events than any run in Darkest Dungeon 2. The combat is confusing and almost impossible to tell what is happening even with tactical pause. Hope you enjoy randomly having all of your shots miss because there's a tiny red circle in the back of two dozen other red circles that provides an insane dodge chance. Hope you enjoy randomly having all of your ships get EMP'd and not be able to shoot down the FIFTEEN nukes that a boss sends your way. I cannot emphasize enough how ridiculous the "tactical level" combat and "strategic level" RNG events are unpleasant to sit through at best and a complete waste of time at worst. Do yourself a favor and skip this game. If the gameplay looks interesting, just play Darkest Dungeon 1 (not 2) or Crying Suns (even though it gets repetitive).
作为一个 BSG 粉，很喜欢这个游戏的氛围。这是个颇有挑战的 roguelike ，有很多有意义的选择，战斗系统也简单明快。钢开始玩的时候可能会觉得比较难，但多玩几把熟悉系统后就能通关了，基本难度通关后，解锁后面的内容才是挑战的地方。 虽然现在没有中文，但文字其实只影响阅读剧情，不影响玩游戏。第一次通关前可能会认真看剧情，后面的挑战基本都无视了。所以有很基础的英文水平就可以很流畅的玩了。

The core game loop is fun. There is a management phase where you have limited turns to deal with problems and gather resources. Then there is a combat phase where you have to survive an onslaught for a time until you can escape. The hero perks and ship upgrades make you feel stronger while also not making the game a cake walk. If you are a fan of the show, the game doesn't do anything to add to that story, but it does capture the feel of the show, especially the first episode of season 1, "33". There are a lot of little touches in the game that show the developers were fans of the show, like the corners being removed from much of the UI and even on the pixelated pieces of paper in the background screens. The rogue lite style works well with the theme of "All of this has happened before, all of it will happen again". All that being said, you don't have to be a fan to enjoy the game and the setting. For anyone who struggles with the game, it has some pretty decent difficulty tweaking. If normal is too hard and easy isn't challenging enough, there is an Assist Mode option that lets you change certain aspects of the combat to your liking, as well as letting you choose to have unlimited retries on battles. Also, the game is about making tough choices. Not every crisis or event can be solved, nor should it be. This is a game I would recommend to anyone that enjoys a challenging rogue lite.
While it is a little repetitive, it keeps you engaged and the battle scenes are fun and in real time.

From the simple-yet-not-easy interface and gameplay, to the games honoring of the design and essence of the 2000's show, Shattered Hopes hits just right as a mix of RPG and RTS. The roguelike elements make it fun to play over again but not so restrictive in its randomness that the path to completion of a run is impossible due to "bad RNG." A definite long term addiction.

FAR too hard, you go from full strength to completely destroyed in 60 seconds. I have gone through the game a few times, replays gives you bonuses from previous runs, I am half way to full bonus for the run and it still takes the piss, too many issues to deal with taking all that bonus resources away making it pointless, then by the time you have to find hidden cylons in your fleet you have no resources to do so. then the combat, the enemy fleet evasion is toooooo HIGH, 120 second battles, you go from 100% health to nothing because you now have 20 enemy ships you cant take down because they all have an evasion buff and 95% of your shots will miss. sure make the game difficult... but put it in the difficult setting, this is all on normal, have not even thought about turning the difficulty up!

Accurate atmosphere, hollow story. It tries to mirror the TV show's suffocating stakes with unforgiving, brutal gameplay, but the narrative ends up feeling incredibly shallow. A licensed game adaptation that nails the vibe but drops the ball on depth.

Half the missions you cannot do (especially kill the Cylons like 'The smart Mission'), repetitive and crappy graphics plus you would think you actually would have something to do with the ship BG.....but know it's just a end game scene.......disappointed

Combat sucks. It's just infested with infiltrators and instagibs so your fighters get nuked with no way to avoid it. Whoo, "strategy game" Hope you like losing the campaign 50 times before normal mode turns into easy mode with all the unlocks you get after losing.

I feel like this game was close but couldn't quite capture what it was trying to do. Too many tedious design choices and repetative tasks. Combats could have been really fun but instead of making them compelling like the show with lots of vipers and carrier craft weapons to all be micro managing they decided to go the opposite direction. If this game did some major overhauls I think it would be worth playing but as it is now I couldn't bring myself to play more.
A brilliant, difficult game that likes to kick you repeatedly.

Excellent FTL-like, with plenty of fanservice for the Battlestar Galactica fans. (None of the characters from the TV show, but everyone rings true.) Discovering bits of story as you complete runs is cool. If you want an easy time, you will need to set the difficulty to Easy. Some of the reviews that complain about the difficulty don't seem to have played the tutorial.
I like the idea, but the game plays like it is run by a DM that keeps forcing hard saves and using loaded dice for repetitive critical misses. Sting-ray, is that you?

Incredible fun. Very moreish like FTL "just one more turn/sector." Really captures the human element of BSG, especially the dialogue and bar interactions. Fans of the show will love this. Frakking cylons.
As its stands after the latest patch, the game is too hard on normal. You will never win unless you have a bucket load of favours.
Have been wishing for a game like this for the last 15 years. I'm a massive BSG fan, and apparently so are the devs.
So say we all.

The core of the game is commanding a squad of 2-4 fighters vs waves of cylons and missle attacks in real time with tacticle pauses , it's midly amsusing but not really my thing. Non the less the reason i gave it a negative review is the meta game built around the core , is aggravating busy work , by the time i got to the cylon spy event and the game gave me this multiple page spread sheet thingy to look over and find the spy i was checked out , the combat is just not that engaging for me to suffer through all the crisis's that pop up between missions.

It's almost good, however there is a problem specifically with certain enemies after a few jumps that super swarm you and have a 90% evasion rate so you have absolutely no chance against them. You have like 2-3 squadrons and the enemy has about 4 times that, under normal circumstances not a problem as you have tactical options, but when your outnumbered forces miss 9 out of every 10 shots, there's really nothing you can do. Especially when they keep spawning more and more units in because you can't kill any of them fast enough. I even had gunstar weapons that shot out like 50 shots at once and it did basically nothing to the enemy forces aside from pop up a bunch of 'miss' notices over them all. It feels like the enemy is cheating, it's so bad. It really makes it seem futile to even try to play the game.

excellent evolution of the Crying Suns formula with a Battlestar Galactica wrapping. It IS a roguelite so frustrating deaths due to running into unfair situations that your force is completely unable to handle is part and parcel of the whole genre really. If you get very aggrieved and frustrated by that sort of thing, you won't like this game. But if you're familiar with roguelites and like the battlestar world this is a fun, solid game.
Not fun. It could be, but it crushes you. Its not strategy. Its just getting stomped.

BSG scattered hopes is an amazing fleet resource management game that I would recommend with the caveat that there are aspects that in it's current form diminishes it's excellent gameplay/replay potential. First off let's awnser the main question I had (and you the reader probably has too) when I read the reviews about this game: "Is the game beatable without the meta progression?" the awnser is a maybe. After a total of 10 runs I was finally able to beat it where I got close to beating it at least 4 times, of which the first time was a part of. The reason I say maybe is because without meta progression your chances of making it through are in the 15% or less. The big reason for this is that meta progression gates many different equipments, talents, squadrons and other aspects from you until you've done certain achievements which is a nice play incentive but as it stands it gates too much. The second big reason your chances are so low is because with meta progression you can start with a ton of resources right of the bat, guaranteeing you that you don't end up in a death spiral immediately as you can of set the costs of potential loses early on. If you like what you've seen so far checkout the amazing demo, of which your progress carries over to the main game. From this point on I will focus on areas of the game I think are lacking after having binged it for multiple hours in a row: 1 this contains spoilers for the story -> [spoiler] after the 4th playthrough it became VERY clear who would always be the cylon, it's one of the two crewmembers that you see at the very beginning of the run. Once you know this all suspense for it dies and it becomes an annoying mechanic, It would be nice if the cylon could be extended to the other canidates or maybe even have a second hidden cylon besides the one on occasions. As it stands this became a very annoying mechanic after I figured that out. [/spoiler] 2 higher tiers in the game don't mean the best upgrades. For example there was a legendary upgrade for one of my squadrons that would allow it to boost its movement speed at the cost of the nuke, which was a very nice buff. So I then skipped it for the rare upgrade of increasing range by 15... This is just one example but I regularly felt that the rarity displays are a visual trap, where I found the less rare upgrades more usefull 90% of the time. 3 Anti missile equipment.. What is up with all the missile destroying equipment, I get it having some of it is nice, but i regularly encounterd multiple equipments who's only function is interfering with missiles, which then became immediately useless because I could already deal with it adequatly thanks to either very fast or long range squadrons or because I had a anti missile civilian ship. Giving some more utility to these equipments so that they do something else besides destroying missiles would be better since they can range from scrap on sight to situational. 4 the reputation system ui it would be nice to get some more clarity in the UI here because as it stands its very frustrating when the game says you've increased reputation a little, what does little mean, sometimes it does nothing sometimes it gets you to the next reputation tier. It feels like I'm being gated in the Ui on where I stand for no reason. If you want to keep the current 5 favor symbol system just make it so that it shows half the shield if your close to progression it. 5 siding with one faction exclusively seems to be less benefical overall compared to just pleasing everyone. I did see there was some kind of buff based on your standing near the end of the run, but frankly at that point it's kind or irrelevant because if you got that far you've already got a decent shot at making it. 6 this is just a pet peeve but it would be nice if there was option in addition to the emergency and normal FTL jump that is something akin to an auto jump option. Basicly when you are ready to leave but need to have your fighters return first it would be nice to have a single button to press that tells all your fighters to return and then have it immediately auto jump when it is done instead of having to pixel time the precise moment where you can jump. It gets very annoying after multiple runs. 7 It would be nice if there was a fleet option to have some of the hero's/squadrons do a training excerise to gain XP, as sometimes you are left in a place with nothing else to do but emergy produce something, which becomes annoying once your overflowing with every resource. 8 Why can't we sell excess supplies/nukes to traders? Your telling me these traders that are cutt of from the rest of humanity wouldn't buy them but would buy scrap?? 9 choices that aren't choices. The game will sometimes offer you choices where a faction will give you a resource reward if you accept and if you don't accept it then you lose reputation with that faction. As far as I can tell there is 0 consequence for taking the resources which makes this a weird choice as either its redunent because there are no drawbacks or there are positives to declining but the game does not telegraph well what these positives actually do. Overall I highly enjoyed my time with the game, but little things like what I mentioned did get annoying on repeated playthroughs and discourage me from replaying the game after having beaten it once.

Is the game ok? Yes, if you just want to waste some time and you do not mind having your time wasted. There are a few design decisions that would make it an excellent gacha. Which makes it not ok, and I would wait for a redesign before purchasing if you are really itching for a roguelite. 1. Crisis flood. Some runs just get destroyed by randomness. You get piled and have NO CHANCE at all to actually play the game or feel like you have any semblance of control. Due to the crisis volume it could be an auto clicker from forced discussion to forced discussion. (Which then drain your resources and you die) 2. Dodgers are a terrible design. You just cannot have AOE in each run because you are not provided the option. So you die. Its not skill or ability of choice. The game just decided this is as far as you go. Because of the above two points its not a good "let off some steam" game. But it also makes sitting down for longer times feel unrewarding when you get destroyed without being able to mount any resistance. Even if you succeed it is just luck then, cause you could do nothing about the loss either so it was not on you when you win. Is the game ok? Sure. Not terrible. Is it genuinely wholeheartedly recommended? Nah.

Game tries to do a lot of things but just doesn't really do them that well. There's a ton of different little mechanics, but all of them are boring. There's a Cylon spy finding minigame that is more-or-less random guessing. The combat is a series of RNG checks that determine if you lose before the battle even starts rather than requiring real strategy. There were no battles where I couldn't tell if I was screwed immediately upon looking at the enemy's innate specials. Events are tedious resource sinks. You're supposed to balance different fleet factions but this is also mostly RNG, since how much influence you gain/lose is obfuscated, and the events are random "Either screw faction A or screw faction B" situations. Runs are much too long and the content is repetitive and uninteresting.

This game does a great job of capturing the atmosphere of the show where nobody is happy, something is always going wrong and the Cylons are always at your heels. It's not a perfect game but the devs are responsive and it's got a lot of fun in it before the seams start to show. Pick up the demo and give it a shot -- it's pretty representative of the final product.

Do not understand why this game isn't at 90+% favorable reviews. It's tense and difficult in a VERY delicious way. Incredible fusion of roguelike with moderately complex RTS that no other developer has come close. This game is dope as ♥♥♥♥ and you should play it.

A couple of negatives that hold this back. First and most important, doing well on a run is purely RNG based, you can mitigate it to a small extent, but ultimately the RNG decides whether or not you will succeed or fail. Second, dialogs. The option to skip dialogs only skips some. I've read all this the first time I went through, your writing is not so captivating as to make me want to read or click past it again, and then click again just to say "yes, I just clicked to close this, really let me close it."

Acceptable core gameplay held back by a lack of interesting story and too much repitition. The developer's previous work, Crying Suns -despite my complaints about its ending- had a captivating story that pushed you forward. You wanted to see what the answer behind the mystery of the great shutdown, and that kept you going. Here there's barely any of that. The mystery of who's a Cylon, so keen in the show, doesn't feel significant when the characters are new each run. The meta story shared between runs is just a few lines long, featuring characters we don't know. The story doesn't keep me playing... ...and neither does the gameplay, which gets same-y pretty quickly. The short-range ships go back and forth. The long range ships sit in place. The battlestar guns clean up stragglers. Let's do that 15 more times this run! The crises, while faithful in concept to the original show, just feel like straightforward resource management exercises. The workers' strike in the show was tense because time was spent showing the conditions, the Chief getting in there and seeing that despite the fleet's dire situation, conditions were still too far gone even for emergency work, and in resolving that it was time for a strike. That makes the crisis feel like a crisis, a choice between two harsh alternatives. A text message saying "Workers say conditions are bad. They want 5 scrap. Pay?" doesn't really feel like anything, not even with the :( face beside it. So, manage some resources for a while, until you get the same story ending cutscene, same as every run. You might unlock a new ship that's actually not quite exactly the same as the previous one but it pretty much is.

I'll tell you upfront: It's a frakkin' ballbuster. But it's fantastic. I can firmly recommend this game, and it rewards repeated runs too with its "Favor" system. You're probably not gonna' win a barenaked first run, do *not* expect to! But you might win your tenth. This is not a bad thing though, because that gives you a LOT of time to get familiar with the systems *and* earn the persistent rewards (which you don't actually HAVE to spend your Favor on, if you don't want to.) The game rewards play. You'll win eventually. Not just from Favor, but from mastering systems, learning what units to use, when and where, and how to manage your fleet and its citizens and their groups to keep everyone something akin to happy. For instance: You may not want to work with the criminal underworld, but you favored the workers against them last time. Unless you want the relationship to become tense, then you better side with the criminals this time, unless you want Underworld related crises to appear... and with the Cylons breathing down your neck? No, you do not want that. Keep everyone as happy as you can. You'll win eventually. I did.

I have rendezvoused with the Battlestar Galactica finally after my fourth run on normal difficultly. I really enjoy this game. People saying it is similar to FTL are correct, it is also very similar to the beginning of Season 1 of the show! The concept is very well executed. I feel like I'm pushing a fleet and its crew to their limits in a mad chase across the galaxy where every jump is a gamble with life and death. I like the resources and gathering, character, fleet, weapon, and squadron mechanics. They are useful, engaging, and add the right amount of depth to the game. I like the reputation mechanic and how the affects if you get/what crisis you get, or boons, but I do not like how negative events have a larger effect than positive events on reputation. I like the crisis and boon quests themselves too. There are some crisis that are easy, some that are arduous. While there are a lot of crisis and it can get frustrating to get hit over and over by them, with careful decision making and usage of resources, plus some luck, you can overcome! Makes them feel like a real crisis! I think there should be some additional boon quests with more profound weapon or fleet rewards. I think this game is appropriately difficult, especially since it is supposed to a replayable roguelike (roguelite? idk) EDIT: yeah way too many negative minor situations for how many crisis there are. you need to decrease the amount of minor negative situations there are and add in some positive situations because otherwise there is just no semi-regular way to increase relations with factions

I really wanted to like this game, but ... 1) There is no way to tell a unit to hold fire and don't move. This makes life very, very frustrating on missions with mines. 2) The are unending crises and things that require your attention... including criminals, workers and your own military that are pack of whiny buttheads that won't shut up. To the point where you can't even finish an action with getting interrupted. If it weren't for these two massive annoyances, this would be a really good game.

Mixed thoughts on this game, I like the setting and generally this kind of game. However it doesn't feel particularly finished, QoL issues abound, there's very little background lore so it feels like they've just sloppily slathered the art style and some references over the game that could have been anything. I feel it's missed out some elements as it lacks the RTS of deadlock or say Gothic that would make the combat sections feel more interesting. The ticking down random weapons of the gun star don't feel that interesting and it makes it a pause fest. Something a bit more like a classic FTL experience where you configure the ship or the fallout shelter style the latest trek game did would have made that combat style more interesting by giving some baseline weapons you manage and improve in the non combat phase with only a smaller amount of deployable one offs. And of the one offs the nukes are just annoying, they're an ok concept, but they shouldn't take up a weapon slot if they're going to be a main resource rather than a general ammo resource. Once you have a few runs the events start repeating themselves. And the heroes are a little one dimensional, the bars a good idea, but you only get one and sometimes two chances at events that might or might not be the heroes, it isn't an click the character any time for a conversation that might or might not go somewhere or you can build favor with in smaller ways. The decisions are presented as impactful, but the scenarios are simple "spend x type of resource to solve" there a few deeper interactions, but its too RNG not RPG to be truly enjoyable. Some of the combat ends up very similar, the diversity of new ships even if they totally lack any interesting lore to read does add character, but sometimes they're just too random and there's no real way to counter if you don't have the right tools. Having a diversity of ships always available and you have to adapt on the fly with them to counter things like electronic warfare style effects would be interesting, and even having more use of pause to have to do something to make that work in some kind of minigame would make it at least skill based. As it stands however you can get RNG'd with an unkillable enemy configuration because it can spam unkillable ships. This feels a bit like a very mature alpha or beta of a game that has had BSG slapped over it. There's certainly some good bits of the game, but there are games that do this better and the combination of things they've borrow to build this version is the wrong combination, or at least not implemented well enough or deep enough to be the right combination. Ultimately you end up with something that feels a bit shallow that could have been a mobile or browser game. Hopefully they fix it, but I'm pretty disappointed with it and I kind of wish I had played a demo first as I don't think I would have bought it at launch if I really understood it. It also frustratingly made me want to go play deadlock, and then get even more frustrated I couldn't go buy the DLC for it as the license has clearly been pulled, which frankly should be illegal and I've no doubt will happen to this game.

This downvote is from the reason why I'm quitting this game. Trying manage relations with the factions is too obscure. I promote a faction 3 times and then get an opportunity with them. Do a single thing that makes them mad and now they are tense. Takes three more positives to balance out a single bad thing. But not always. I feel the value of faction increase and decrease are not fixed but they are hidden. It feels arbitrary.
My run came to a screeching halt because the enemy kept spamming a boat-load of beacons that gave all their ships 90% dodge.

The game can be fun, but it's also so punishing at times with wicked RNG that it's just not fun. The kind of game that you just quit and don't want to play anymore, because it's so hard it's not enjoyable. It's been about 50/50 for me. Easy difficulty is more like a typical 'normal' and normal is more like 'hardcore'. It needs balance tweaks, and some mechanics make zero sense. One gunstar start comes with a missile defense ship that can shoot down one enemy missile every 13-20 seconds. BUT, if you piss off the underworld they take over the ship and you have to try and board it. In that mission, it can suddenly fire about 5 missiles per second and it's pretty much impossible to beat the mission. Then it's -1000 gunstar health. Enemy evasion is ridiculous at times too. Invisible ships, etc. I wish there way a way to just have raiders and heavy raiders. You will be dealing with some crisis or pop up almost every turn. Most 'shops' have ridiculous prices. It might be armageddon, but they still will price gouge the ♥♥♥♥ out of you so you can't even buy cool stuff just to experiment with it. If you like games where you are forced to fail many times, this is the game for you.

As is evident in my playtime, big fan of the game. It released with quite a few bugs, but they're addressed now. The devs have made a few balance changes (the community provides feedback in the discord), but I grinded out the game to my satisfaction before anything was fixed. I'm a huge fan of the series and they did well to capture its tone within a roguelite. With the format naturally comes a level of formula to the narrative events and crises, but once you've seen an event, you have the option to skip dialogue and go straight to the crisis decision. The devs are still fixing the balance of faction influences and maintenance/healthcare levels and, with enough interest, have shown openness to adding more content for us franchise diehards (say, more narrative paths, fleets, powers, rewards). The core gameplay loop is fulfilling and varied. As with any game, once you've invested the amount of time I have, you'll be able to construct a tier list of weak and strong options. This is part of the fun of discovering and figuring things out. True, dodgers are insanely annoying and unfair -- deal with it.
